posts.text: The other extremely frustrating thing is that there is no unified theory. One person claims "fraud" because of Dominion hacking the election. Another person thinks it was ballot stuffing (a la "2,000 mules"). Another person says "the statistical impossibility," i.e. they don't know *how* it was stolen they just know it was. Another person focused only on Georgia and Fulton County, while another focuses on the Rust Belt and Pennsylvania. Some people blame Facebook and Covid-era mail-in voting rul

It has been a year or so since I was in the trenches on the election fraud claims, and I forgot how frustrating the pattern can be:

> person makes claim about fraud
> explain how you know the claim is misleading or invented
> person says claim never got heard by the courts
> explain how the claim was investigated by LEO or heard before a judge or a court and then got dismissed
> person says LEO/judge/courts are corrupt and in on the scheme
> explain that there are pro-Trump LE

O'Donnell is a software engineer funded by Mike Lindell who is making absolutely CASH off selling these ridiculous documentaries claiming "algorithmic vote manipulation" which he's been unable to get a single other person or organization to verify. He is an activist hack stealing your money. Please don't pay to watch his stuff.

Leah Hoopes and Greg Stenstrom went to court with their claims that they witnessed fraud firsthand (plugging in unauthorized USB drives) and their cases were shredded. Q

Since I published my 6,000-word piece on the Trump dealing literally two weeks ago, I've seen another dozen or so stories just as obvious and brazen as this one. It's stunning.


Judd Legum (@JuddLegum)

1. On March 11, Trump toured a Thermo Fisher Scientific facility in Ohio and repeatedly praised the company. 

On *the same day* Trump bought between $15,000 and $50,000 of Thermo Fisher stock.

This is a great example of election fraud stuff where the truth takes actual explaining while the lie/exaggeration is simple, quippy, and made for social media.

Real: Fulton County admitted that ~315,000 early votes were certified without required poll worker signatures on tabulator tapes. This is an actual procedural violation. The State Election Board voted 3-0 to refer it to the AG's office, and someone is likely getting fined (not jail, bc it wasn't criminal).

I will make a deal: If you are in these comments claiming there is evidence that the 2020 election was stolen, present it. If you show me the evidence and it actually stumps me — I can't explain it, I can't debunk it, I can't show you why it's nonsense — I'll Venmo you $1,000.

If you are here to tell me that the evidence is forthcoming or that you saw some video but you can't find it or that these cases never got their day in court, I am not going to respond to you. I will also not reply to anything covered in my previous writing. 

archive.skeptic.com/archive/…

It has been six years. Every single "stolen election" theory — from 2,000 Mules to servers in Italy to Georgia suitcases — has been debunked, crushed in court, painstakingly explained, and none of these guys ever have the goods cause it's all nonsense to please POTUS. It's embarrassing for Bartiromo that she is still giving this airtime, and anyone who still falls for this chasing the next new reveal needs to get away from their computer.


Aaron Rupar (@atrupar)
